Recorded as INDIRECT because the step is not demonstrated: the source that describes both ends says there is a gap between them. The edge is drawn so the graph reaches the clinical syndrome, and the gap is a discussion rather than a hidden assumption.

Headache with the ataxia is what marks the tiers in which the cerebellum is swollen. No cited source states the mechanism, so the edge is drawn through unknown intermediates: raised pressure in the posterior fossa is the obvious route and none of these papers measures it.
The other half of the pair that marks those tiers, and on the same footing: an association the cited sources report without measuring what lies between.

Swelling in the posterior fossa obstructs cerebrospinal fluid outflow. No cited source states the hydrodynamics: the sources that link the swelling to hydrocephalus do so without describing how the outflow is blocked.

Chickenpox is one of the infections that precede the syndrome. Counted from the syndrome's side, it came before a third of the cases in the Dutch national surveillance study; counted from the virus's side, acute cerebellar ataxia was the commonest neurological complication of the virus in a children's hospital series.

Epstein-Barr virus infection is one of the infections that precede the syndrome. In both adult reports the virus was found in the blood while testing of the cerebrospinal fluid for it was negative; the authors of one favour a post-infectious reading and add that serology is not the best test.
Drawn without an effect predicate. The work-up of one child found the virus, which places it beside the syndrome but does not show that it was the trigger.
Drawn without an effect predicate. The one case cited carried a second virus at the same time.

Acts on the varicella share of the preceding infections only; it has no bearing on the other triggers. No cited source measures the syndrome's incidence before and after a vaccination programme, so the effect rests on a projection from two rates, on a fall in the neurological complications of varicella as a whole, and on what is seen in a vaccinated population.

nodes.description: The humoral arm of the immune response, as far as it can be measured: antibodies in serum or cerebrospinal fluid that bind brain tissue or named neural antigens. The targets differ between patients and studies: glutamate receptor delta 2, a receptor of the Purkinje cell, in single cases; centrosome proteins, pericentrin among them, after varicella; and neuronal, glial and myelin antigens in 10 of 36 children with acute cerebellitis in one multicentre series. No study cited here found a single antigen targeted in most of its patients. Antibodies against centrosome proteins are found after varicella without ataxia as well, though not those against pericentrin. Whether any of them injures the cerebellum, rather than marking an injury already done, is not settled; the node has no edge onward for that reason, and the question is recorded in the discussions.

nodes.description: The step that makes this disease immune-mediated rather than infectious. Not every cited source names an immune mechanism: several describe the disease without one, and one of them calls the aetiology usually viral. It places the syndrome in the family of immune-mediated cerebellar ataxias, beside gluten ataxia, the paraneoplastic degenerations and opsoclonus-myoclonus. Which effector does the damage is not settled here: autoantibodies against several cerebellar targets are reported in individual patients, and whether any of them is pathogenic rather than a consequence of damage is an open question recorded in this entry's discussions.

nodes.description: The consequence of posterior fossa swelling, and the reason the fulminant tier may need cerebrospinal fluid diversion. Several cited sources call it obstructive hydrocephalus in those words. HPO's nearest narrower term is Noncommunicating hydrocephalus, HP:0010953, and the two are not the same concept: asked directly, OLS returns no exact synonym for that term at all, and HPO's own definition says the most common form of noncommunicating hydrocephalus is obstructive, which makes obstructive a subset rather than a synonym. nodes.description: An infection, or rarely a vaccination, precedes the cerebellar syndrome by a latent interval of about a week. No single organism defines it: the commonest trigger differs by era and population, and in a quarter of children none is identified.

evidence.reference_title: Acute Cerebellar Inflammation and Related Ataxia: Mechanisms and Pathophysiology.
evidence.snippet: In our animal model of the acute inflammation of the cerebellar cortex, animals did not show any ataxia but hyperexcitability in the cerebellar cortex and depression-like behaviors. In contrast, animal models with neurodegeneration of the cerebellar Purkinje cells and hypoexcitability of the neurons show cerebellar ataxia. The suppression of the Ca2+-activated K+ channels in vivo is associated with a type of ataxia. Therefore, there is a gap in our interpretation between the very early phase of cerebellar inflammation and the emergence of cerebellar ataxia.

nodes.description: Protects against the varicella share of the syndrome. In a national Australian surveillance series from a population with high vaccine coverage, none of 20 cases followed varicella. The vaccine itself is reported before onset far more rarely than the infection: a Dutch study sets a reporting rate of 0.15 per 100,000 vaccine doses against 5 cases per 100,000 infections in young children, though its abstract does not say where the per-dose figure was measured.
